title: Grammar Foundations: Present Simple and Sentence Order
sourceNote: Original EnglishCode practice examples. Exercise formats are informed by the publicly described categories in Grammar-Drill-Yard; no upstream code or lesson content is copied.

options.text: She go to work by bus.
She goes to work by bus.
She going to work by bus.

items.feedback: Use -s with he, she, and it in the present simple.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: My brother ___ (study) English every evening.
items.feedback: For consonant + y, change y to -ies.

items.prompt: Put the words in a natural sentence.
items.feedback: A common neutral order is subject, adverb of frequency, verb, object, then time.

items.instruction: Write a negative sentence with the same meaning.
items.feedback: Keep the verb be; do not add do/does.

items.prompt: Find and correct the grammar error.
items.sourceText: He go to school every day.
items.correctedText: He goes to school every day.
items.explanation: In the present simple, a third-person singular subject takes -s or -es.

items.prompt: Match each word with its closest meaning.
Recall the meaning before revealing the answer.
items.back: Able to be trusted or depended on.
